sentences.text: If you dig a hole in the yard and pour water in, you have a pool.
But the thirsty soil drinks all 20,000 gallons, and the hole drains dry.
The pit sits empty, and the wet dirt slumps off its walls.
But soaked soil is heavy, so the wall of the hole cracks.
So you pour a concrete floor and thick walls to hold the dirt back.
But concrete drinks water too, so you lay a blue liner over it.
Now you fill the sealed shell, and the water finally stays.
But still water goes bad, so you add a pump and pipes to keep it moving.
This is a swimming pool.
Its pump and pipes are a filtration system.
Water leaves through a drain, passes the filter, and returns clean through a jet.
Every drop makes a full trip through the filter about once every eight hours.
So the pump pushes about 2,500 gallons an hour through one pipe.
But the sun warms the water, algae grows, and the pool turns green.
Then a storm adds rain, and the green pool overflows across the lawn.
So you add chlorine to clear the algae, and a drain to carry the extra water away.
And the blue water everyone knows is not blue, so we drain it and leave only the liner.
Water absorbs red light, so deep pool water looks blue, and the liner does the rest.
Add rocks round the edge, steps into the water, and a light.
Congratulations, you have built a swimming pool.
